summary: Lunar Mission Control is an interactive, decision-support web platform engineered for lunar south pole exploration, aligning with NASA’s Artemis objectives. Developed for the LUNEX Team during the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge, our solution solves the critical operational triad of lunar landing site selection by integrating real-time solar illumination metrics, Earth line-of-sight communications visibility, and synthetic terrain-hazard modeling into a unified dashboard. Using Skyfield and the NASA JPL DE421 ephemeris, the platform evaluates candidate regions (such as Shackleton and de Gerlache rims), features an interactive rover battery survival simulator, renders 3D crater topography, and provides a multi-parameter candidate leaderboard to guide future sustainable lunar surface operations.
details:
> What it does & How it works:

> Lunar Mission Control acts as a comprehensive mission-planning dashboard that enables users and mission planners to screen and compare candidate lunar south pole landing regions. The application evaluates candidate sites using a weighted scoring model: 40% direct-to-Earth communications visibility, 30% solar illumination for power availability, and 30% terrain safety based on slope and rock hazards. It features a dynamic site selector, interactive telemetry charts (Sun/Earth elevation and horizon profiles), a 100% to shadowed-depletion rover battery survival model, and a coordinate-dependent 3D crater topography visualizer.

> Tech Stack & Tools Used:

> * Programming & Core Logic: Python 3.12, NumPy, Pandas, Matplotlib, Plotly.

> * Astronomy & Ephemeris Engine: Skyfield library powered by the NASA JPL DE421 ephemeris (de421.bsp, pck00008.tpc, and lunar orientation data).

> * Web Interface & Deployment: Streamlit for the interactive dashboard UI, hosted and deployed live via Streamlit Cloud and GitHub.

>

>

> Intended Impact & Creativity:

> The project bridges complex orbital mechanics and practical mission design into an accessible tool. By consolidating power, communication, and terrain constraints into an intuitive interface, it empowers researchers and engineers to make rapid, data-driven decisions for future crewed and robotic Artemis missions to the lunar south pole.
